points.description: States that a constructor is called automatically/implicitly whenever an object is created (instantiated), whereas a function must be called explicitly by the programmer.
points.partial_credit: Half (1.25) if only one side is precise, e.g. constructor is called automatically on object creation but the explicit calling of functions is not stated.

points.description: States that a constructor has no return type (not even void), whereas a function must declare/indicate a return type.
points.partial_credit: Half (1.25) if only one side is stated precisely, e.g. constructors have no return type but the requirement for functions to declare one is missing.

rubric.notes: Full marks need both differences stated precisely as contrasts: automatic call on object creation vs explicit call for functions, and no return type for constructors vs a required return type for functions. Vague statements (e.g. "constructor initialises objects", "functions do tasks") earn nothing. Any wrong claim within a point, such as saying constructors return a value or have return type void, loses that point.
